recipes.title: Three-body and few-body gravity (chaos, choreographies)
recipes.adapt: Other presets: psim presets. Custom bodies: write a scenario JSON (references/gravity.md) and use --scenario. No code needed.
recipes.summary: Three bodies pulling on each other: chaos, choreographies, near-collisions.
recipes.checked: Kepler orbit, figure-eight period, Pythagorean outcome; energy error ~10⁻¹¹
recipes.prompt: simulate three stars orbiting each other

recipes.title: Solar System / planets orbiting the Sun (JPL elements, J2000)
recipes.adapt: Subset: --planets Earth,Mars,Jupiter --years 20. Exoplanets or moons: a scenario JSON in AU, M☉, yr (G = G_AU_MSUN_YR ≈ 4π²). No code needed.
recipes.summary: The Sun and eight planets from JPL orbital elements, every planet pulling on every other.
recipes.checked: Earth’s J2000 position (JPL), Mars’ period, Earth’s year
recipes.prompt: model the planets orbiting the Sun

recipes.title: Charged particle in electric and magnetic fields (relativistic Boris pusher)
recipes.adapt: Electron/ion: change the mass/charge constants in physics.mjs (core/constants.mjs). Non-uniform fields: replace E and Bv with functions of x inside step(); keep the Boris update and the verify() checks that still apply.
recipes.summary: A proton spiralling through a magnetic field, relativistic, with an optional E×B drift.
recipes.checked: Exact gyroradius, 1 GeV gyroperiod, drift speed
recipes.prompt: simulate a proton moving through a magnetic field

recipes.title: Black-body radiation, colour of hot objects, Planck / Wien / Stefan–Boltzmann
recipes.adapt: Everything is in core/radiation.mjs. Add presets or plots in page.html; workbench layout with term-split equations is already set up.
recipes.summary: Planck’s law and the true colour of hot objects, from a candle to a blue star.
recipes.checked: CODATA constants, solar constant 1361 W/m², CMB peak 160.2 GHz

recipes.title: Black hole: event horizon, shadow, gravitational lensing, accretion disk (GPU ray tracing)
recipes.adapt: Lensing of a background source or Einstein rings: keep the shader, change the sky function (uSky branch) to draw the source; deflection, capture and shadow are already exact (core/schwarzschild.mjs: tracePhoton, deflectionExact, shadowAngle). Keep window.psim.selfTest.
recipes.summary: Light traced through Einstein’s geometry on your GPU: shadow, photon ring, lensed accretion disk.
recipes.checked: Exact shadow size (GPU within 1 px), light bending at the Sun 1.751″
recipes.prompt: simulate a black hole event horizon

recipes.title: Galaxy rotation and dark matter (stars in a Milky-Way mass model)
recipes.adapt: Other galaxies: change the normalisation in core/galaxy.mjs normalise({ v, R, fBulge, fDisk, fHalo }) or the component scales; the rotation-curve plot and equation update automatically.
recipes.summary: Thousands of stars in a Milky-Way model. Switch dark matter off and watch the galaxy fly apart.
recipes.checked: Bovy (2015) model, measured rotation curve (Eilers et al. 2019)
recipes.prompt: show why galaxies need dark matter

recipes.title: GPS and relativity: clock time dilation from gravity and speed
recipes.adapt: Other orbits (ISS, Galileo, geostationary): change the a/e defaults. Other bodies: GM and the ground potential in core/relativity.mjs. Twin paradox: reuse orbitRateTerms for a moving clock.
recipes.summary: Why GPS satellite clocks run 38 µs/day fast: gravity and speed, side by side.
recipes.checked: GPS specification: 10.22999999543 MHz, F constant; IAU L_G
recipes.prompt: how does relativity affect GPS clocks?
